Although the proof is inspired by the non-fractional argument of Ombrosi, Rivera-Ríos and Safe in \cite{ORRS}, the fractional normalization introduces a genuinely new scale interaction. At radius $r$, one must renormalize the function by $k^{rα}$ while keeping the dyadic cutoff at $k^r$; this leads to a new summation mechanism involving simultaneously $k^{rα}$ and $k^{r(1-α)}$. We then study sharpness and the geometry of admissible weights. We construct counterexamples showing that the estimate cannot in general be reduced to $s=1$ for any $0<α<1$. In the subcritical range $0<α<1/2$, we characterize power-type radial weights satisfying the natural fractional $A_1$ condition and prove that the failure persists after any fixed finite number of iterations of $M_α$. We also prove that $M_αw\lesssim w$ is necessary for the corresponding weighted weak type estimate but is not sufficient in the subcritical range. Finally, we identify a phase transition: for $1/2\leα<1$ no nonzero global weight can satisfy $M_αw\lesssim w$.

papers.title: Sign-hedged Beam QAOA:Scaling Quantum Optimization Algorithms
papers.abstract: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) encodes a combinatorial objective as an Ising Hamiltonian and alternates cost and mixer operations for p rounds. Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) scales further by using the resulting correlations, whether variables tend to agree or disagree, to eliminate variables one at a time. But each inferred sign is accepted irrevocably, so a single early mistake propagates through every later reduction and can discard the global optimum. As elimination proceeds, residuals shrink while effective edge density typically rises, so later decisions face denser Ising problems, a regime that fully connected Sherrington Kirkpatrick (SK) instances stress test directly. This paper proposes sign-hedged beam RQAOA, which retains the variable or pair selected by standard RQAOA, explores both possible sign assignments, keeps the best B residual problems according to a classical score, and completes each survivor with ordinary RQAOA. On frustrated SK instances, where standard recursion collapses to AR 0.474, beam recovers near-optimal AR 0.998 at the same p. We evaluate the workflow on 50+ instances from HamLib and QOBLIB, spanning 4 and 5 regular and Erdos Renyi MaxCut graphs, Sherrington Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glasses, and cardinality-constrained portfolio optimization, with up to 60 qubits and hardware runs on ibm kingston and ibm marrakesh. Matched simulator and device cells show consistent beam rankings: simulation and hardware agree that beam recovers near-optimal approximation ratio (AR) where standard recursion fails. These gains come from additional residual-circuit evaluations, classical pruning, and exact solution of a small core, rather than from increasing p, beam is a decision-side optimization atop fixed-p QAOA/RQAOA, not a claim that quantum circuits alone scale with qubit count.

papers.title: Branch-Extended Automatic Differentiation
papers.abstract: We present branch-extended automatic differentiation (BEAD), a software package that provides information about inactive branches of piecewise-differentiable functions, intended for use in nonsmooth optimization algorithms. BEAD is implemented in Python, building on the popular JAX framework. For supported nonsmooth operations such as abs and max, BEAD identifies alternative branches within tolerance from the given input, and computes gradients of the resulting branches extended to the given input. Such information has been previously used for robust optimization methods, but has required error-prone and tedious manual differentiation, unlike BEAD, which is fully automated for functions written in NumPy-like JAX code. Our experiments show that our approach is as accurate as manually written derivative code, and offers more flexibility in modifying the function and choosing between branch-discovery rules. While we were originally motivated by the manifold sampling algorithm for nonsmooth composite objectives, we also integrate BEAD branch-extension gradients into a nonsmooth BFGS-SQP solver. On two small nonsmooth test problems, the resulting path-aware search resolves failures or substantially reduces the number of evaluations required by the BFGS-SQP solver.

papers.title: Regularity of elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure
papers.abstract: We study autonomous elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure of the form \[ -\operatorname{div}\big(\mathfrak a(|Du|)Du\big)=0 \quad \text{in }\ Ω\subset \mathbb R^n \] Under two-sided quantitative $(p,q)$-growth conditions on $\mathfrak a$, we prove gradient Hölder continuity with constants and exponent depending only on the dimensions, $p$ and $q$. This improves the classical theory initiated by Uhlenbeck by removing the continuity requirement on $\mathfrak a'$. The proof uses nonlinear comparison systems whose regularity follows from a scalar uniformly elliptic equation. Under weaker $(p,q)$-growth conditions on the convex function $\varphi(t):=\int_0^t s\mathfrak a(s)\,ds$, we obtain local $W^{1,s}$-regularity for every $s>1$, and hence Hölder continuity of solutions with every exponent less than one. An additional lower growth condition on $\mathfrak a$ yields local Lipschitz continuity, even when $\mathfrak a$ is discontinuous.

papers.title: How Many Shots Does a Quantum Reservoir Need? Measurement Cost and Its Scaling in Buffered Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) inherits from classical reservoir computing the property that only a linear readout is trained, but unlike a classical reservoir its state is never directly observable: every feature is an expectation value estimated from a finite number of measurement shots. The shot budget is therefore a first-class hyperparameter with no classical analogue. Its effect on QRC has recently begun to be studied; what remains unsettled is how a required budget should be defined, and whether competing definitions agree. This paper argues that they do not, and that the disagreement is systematic rather than incidental. This paper distinguishes a \emph{precision budget} $N_\varepsilon$, the shots needed to estimate the reservoir features to a fixed relative accuracy, from a \emph{convergence budget} $N_\star$, the shots needed for the trained readout to approach its own noise-free ceiling. Proposition~\ref{prop:confound} shows that $N_\star$ depends on the noise-free error floor by construction, so that a configuration with a worse floor appears cheaper, and that configurations should therefore be compared at a fixed measurement budget rather than by the budget each needs to reach its own ceiling.

papers.title: Evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields
papers.abstract: We extend the auxiliary-field method for scattered subspaces to evasive subspaces and subspace designs. For $1\le h\le k<hn$ and coprime $h,k+1$ with $n(k-h+1)\ge k+1$, we construct spanning $(h,k)$-evasive $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^r$ of dimension $rn(k-h+1)/(k+1)$ in every sufficiently large admissible ambient dimension, with a threshold independent of $q$. When $k<n$, this dimension is maximum. The proof combines an intersection lemma, a rank-support density inequality, scalar orbit counting, and a profile preserved by direct sums. The coding consequences include, for every fixed odd extension degree $m\ge3$ and every sufficiently large $K$, minimal rank-metric codes of optimal length $2K$ with first two generalized weights $(m+1)/2$ and $m+1$. For these codes the stable profile is equivalent to minimality with the largest possible minimum distance; for even $m$ the analogous class consists of minimal MRD codes. More generally, for $1\leτ\le m-2$ and $\gcd(m,τ+1)=1$, we obtain nondegenerate $τ$-minimal codes of length $(τ+1)K$ for every sufficiently large $K$, uniformly in $q$. We also construct maximum $h$-designs whose number of members grows exponentially with the ambient dimension at fixed $q,n,h$, and the associated maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes with a growing number of equal long blocks. In extension degree five, the ordinary and $2$-minimal constructions hold for every $q$ and every $K\ge32$ and $K\ge59$, respectively.

papers.title: Singularities and Collision Criteria in the Gravitational Straight-Segment Problem with Arbitrary Positive Density
papers.abstract: We study singularities and collision criteria for a massless particle around a fixed finite straight segment with an arbitrary positive continuous density. We first show that every singularity forces the trajectory to approach the material segment. Using the axial symmetry of the potential, we prove that any trajectory approaching the segment is confined to an invariant plane containing it. Moreover, we show that every singularity is either a collision singularity or an ejection singularity. Finally, in the invariant plane, we introduce an angular-cone condition for positions and momenta directed toward the segment. We prove that if the initial position-momentum pair belongs to the angular cone, then the trajectory collides with the segment in finite time, and we derive an upper bound for the collision time. We further prove that the final arc of any collision satisfies the angular-cone condition.

papers.title: Nonzero solutions for Dirichlet problems with the competing (p,q)-Laplacian
papers.abstract: The following equation is considered: $$-Δ_p u(\boldsymbol{x}) + Δ_q u(\boldsymbol{x}) = f\big(\boldsymbol{x}, u(\boldsymbol{x})\big)\text{ for } \boldsymbol{x} \in Ω, \qquad u(\boldsymbol{x}) = 0 \text{ for } \boldsymbol{x}\in \partial Ω.$$ We start by showing that the energy functional associated with the considered problem no longer has the properties typical of its non-competing counterpart, which prevents a direct application of standard variational and monotonicity methods. Using Ekeland's variational principle combined with properties imposed on the nonlinear term~$f$, we prove the existence of a nonzero generalized solution to the problem. It is also shown that in the one-dimensional case $Ω= (-1,1)$, assuming that $f$ satisfies the symmetry conditions $$f(x,u) = f(-x,u) = -f(x,-u),$$ together with the sign condition $f(x,u) \geq 0$ for $u \geq 0$ and an appropriate growth bound on $f$, a convex relaxation of the action functional yields the existence of a positive weak solution. Furthermore, we prove that in this setting, and under a slightly stronger sign condition $$f(x,u) > 0\text{ for }u > 0,$$ all global minimizers of the action functional do not vanish in $(-1,1)$ but fail to be of class $C^1$.

papers.title: A tractable transition function for the Wright-Fisher diffusion with selection via gamma duality
papers.abstract: The transition function of the Wright-Fisher diffusion with selection is a fundamental object for non-neutral evolutionary modelling and likelihood-based inference, but, unlike in the neutral case, existing representations are impractical or inefficient. Spectral approaches rely on truncation levels that grow with selection strength and the number of alleles, thus leading to rapidly increasing computational costs, while existing duality-based expansions lead to multi-type dual processes whose transition probabilities involve intractable normalising constants. In this paper we obtain a new transition-function representation for the multi-allelic Wright-Fisher diffusion with parent-independent mutation and genic selection that makes transition-law evaluation and simulation practically feasible in regimes where existing methods are costly or unavailable. The key tool is a new gamma duality, obtained by augmenting classical polynomial duality by an exponential tilting and yields a multivariate birth-death dual with fully explicit infinitesimal rates and an entrance-boundary construction. This is used to express the Wright-Fisher transition law as an explicit mixture of standard Dirichlet components, with mixing weights obtained from the dual started from its entrance boundary. We characterise the dual stationary distribution and its small-time behaviour, and develop practical and efficient sampling procedures for both transition and stationary laws, including a fast approximate stationary sampler with explicit error control. Numerical experiments illustrate substantial runtime gains over specialised methods in regimes where they apply, while our approach remains applicable for arbitrary numbers of alleles and selection coefficients.

papers.title: What are local complementations, really?
papers.abstract: A local complementation at a vertex $v$ of a graph $G$ replaces the induced neighborhood of $v$ with its complement. Local complementations are, at face value, peculiar operations. Yet they famously show up when describing the local Clifford equivalence among graph states, and, because of this, have become a fundamental notion in the study of graph states. Following Bouchet, we show here how local complementations on graphs are more naturally thought of in terms of switchings of (matroid) bases of stabilizer states. Bases and switchings reveal structural properties of stabilizer states that are harder to glean from the graph-theoretic description alone, such as vertex-minors and statistics of local Pauli measurements. Bases also simplify prior proofs about graphs up to local complementations, of which we give several examples. Bases are foundational in the study of (multi)matroids; as such this paper serves as a gentle introduction to the applications of multimatroids to quantum information theory.

papers.title: Quantum-enabled measurement of gravitational forces at the milligram scale
papers.abstract: Gravity is by far the weakest among all known interactions. While it dominates the large-scale structure of the universe, gravitational interactions between small masses in the microscopic range remain underexplored because they are too weak to be experimentally accessible. The interface between gravity, described by general relativity, and quantum mechanics, which describes the microscopic world, is of particular interest. From a theory standpoint, these two major descriptions of nature have not been combined in a satisfactory manner. Technology is gradually becoming mature enough such that probing gravity at the microscopic scale, where quantum mechanics and gravity potentially meet, is becoming accessible. Explorations towards genuine quantum gravity have to be carried out under conditions where the gravitating masses possess non-classical properties, which necessitates ultimate protection against disturbances, such as ultralow temperatures and a small range of motion. Here, we present an experiment at millikelvin temperatures, where the gravity due to a micron-range coherent displacement of an 87 mg source mass imprints on the motion of an oscillating membrane loaded with a 1.3 mg test mass. Vibrations of the membrane are measured in the microwave optomechanical scheme, which is a key setup for investigating non-classical motional states of mechanical oscillators. When considering the combination of total source and test masses, our setup presents two orders of magnitude progress in sensing gravity at the small scale, as well as a 35 dB improvement of gravitational sensitivity at kHz frequencies or above. Our setup offers a plausible approach for studying gravitational interactions between masses prepared in non-classical motional states.

papers.title: How the $p$-Bergman metric approaches the Carathéodory metric
papers.abstract: We study the rate at which the $p$-Bergman metric approaches the Carathéodory metric on convex domains with measures comparable to $δ^αdV$, $α>-1$. On smooth convex domains of finite type the logarithmic coefficient is bounded above by the harmonic-measure average of the tangential multitype dimension plus $1+α$, with equality when almost every endpoint of the extremal disc is coercive. For a class of convex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with $C^4$ boundary and rank-one real tangential contact along an axis disc, a winding number distinguishes the coefficient $2+α$ from an upper bound $7/4+α$; quartic contact makes the latter bound exact. The exact value holds along the entire axis of explicit real-algebraic strongly pseudoconvex domains, including perturbations without the weighted circle action, although their pointwise boundary models agree up to unitary equivalence with those of a domain having coefficient $2+α$. A $C^2$ example has negative winding but coefficient $2+α$, with a $-\frac12\log\log p$ correction, so boundary regularity is essential to the gap theorem.

papers.title: Interacting Urn Schemes on Infinite Graphs: A Representation Approach
papers.abstract: Interacting urn schemes have emerged as an important framework for studying reinforcement phenomena in interacting stochastic systems (see, e.g., \cite{launay2011interacting,launay2012generalized,WARM2014,aletti2017interacting,Synchronisation-2,kaur2023interacting,kaur2023interacting2}). Most existing results, however, are restricted to finite systems. In this article, we investigate interacting urn schemes involving infinitely many urns, where the interactions are naturally described by a directed graph. The reinforcement or drawing mechanism at each urn depends on the compositions of its in-neighboring urns. To analyze the asymptotic behavior of these systems, we develop a representation of the urn dynamics in terms of branching Markov processes evolving on a class of random forests introduced in this article. This extends the representation approach of \cite{bandyopadhyay2022new}, originally developed for single Pólya urn schemes, to interacting urn schemes on locally finite directed graphs. Using this representation, we establish almost sure convergence of the color proportions under standard conditions on the reinforcement matrix or kernel. In particular, we show that the convergence holds independently of the topology of the underlying graph, and hence our results also apply to undirected graphs, where the interactions are bidirectional. We further investigate measure-valued generalizations and other related reinforced stochastic processes, illustrating the broad applicability of the representation approach. Finally, we discuss connections with self-organized criticality.

papers.title: The Gibbons--Penrose inequality in Minkowski spacetime
papers.abstract: We prove the Gibbons--Penrose inequality for smooth closed spacelike codimension-two submanifolds of Minkowski spacetime whose past null second fundamental form is non-negative. The proof is motivated by the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci technique.

papers.title: Gaussian fluctuations of the moderately interacting Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto particle system around the mollified mean-field limit
papers.abstract: We study, at the logarithmic mollification scale $η^{-2(d+1+α)}\leδ\log N$ of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, the fluctuation field $V^N=\sqrt N(μ^N-u_η)$ of the moderately interacting multi-species particle system whose mean-field limit is the Shigesada- Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system. The field is centred at the solution $u_η$ of the mollified equation, which depends on $N$ through $η$. On a scale of weighted Bessel-potential spaces of negative order we prove that the laws of $(V^N,M^N)$ are tight, where $M^N$ is the martingale part. Every limit point of $M^N$ is a continuous Gaussian martingale with an explicit deterministic bracket. Every limit point of $V^N$ is a weak solution, and the mild solution, of a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SPDE whose drift is the linearisation of the SKT operator at the limit $u$. The initial field and the martingale are independent, and weak solutions are unique given both, so the whole sequence converges in law, jointly with the martingale part, and the limit is unique in law among solutions of the martingale problem. The noise is $d M_i=div(\sqrt{2u_iΘ_i}dW_i)$, with $Θ_i=σ_i+\sum_jf(a_{ij}u_j)$ and $W$ a cylindrical Wiener process on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^{nd})$. The hypotheses are those of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, including the smallness and the nonnegativity on $\mathbb{R}$ of the nonlinearity $f$. We add radial kernels $B_{ij}$, the independence of the initial data and the Brownian motions across particles and species, a smaller $δ$, a regularity budget on $u_0$, a strengthened smallness condition on $f$ that makes the backward system diagonally dominant in weighted spaces, and an integer Sobolev index $s$.

papers.title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
papers.abstract: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale $c$, with splitting $Δ(c)\propto1/c$. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the $(4+ε)$-dimensional $O(N)$ model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of $N$ through $N=4$ has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.

papers.title: Exploring topological signatures of quantum Fisher information scaling in graph states
papers.abstract: Graph states are a versatile resource for quantum metrology, and their quantum Fisher information (QFI) has a closed-form expression in terms of the underlying graph: it counts pairs of vertices with identical neighborhoods. It remains unclear, however, which global structural properties of a graph determine whether its QFI exceeds the standard quantum limit (SQL). Here we ask whether topological invariants, namely the Betti numbers of the graph's clique complex, capture this behavior, and we address the question numerically with two complementary approaches. First, we randomly add or delete edges in balanced complete multipartite graphs, which combine a QFI beyond the SQL with a single nonvanishing higher Betti number. Edge addition eventually destroys both the metrological advantage and the nontrivial topology. Under edge deletion, by contrast, higher Betti numbers persist well after the QFI has dropped to the SQL. Second, we start from Erdős--Rényi random graphs, whose QFI does not typically exceed the SQL, and maximize a chosen Betti number with a Monte Carlo search. The search drives the graphs toward near-extremal multipartite structures whose QFI lies well beyond the SQL. Our results show that topological optimization offers a route to metrologically useful graph states, but also that Betti numbers alone do not determine the QFI.

papers.title: Weak and strong discretization errors for signatures of Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a continuous Gaussian process in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, with independent components of roughness $H\in(\tfrac14,1)$, possibly with a linear drift, and let $X^n$ be its piecewise-linear interpolant on a mesh of width $δ$. We study how well the truncated signature of $X^n$ approximates that of the natural lift of $X$, in mean (the weak error) and in $L^2$ (the strong error). Over a class of drivers defined by quantitative regularity conditions, the weak error at every fixed truncation level is $O(δ^{γ(H)})$ with $γ(H)=\min(2H,4H-1)$, uniformly over the class, and for truncation levels $M\ge4$ fractional Brownian motion attains this rate. For centred drivers the weak error vanishes at levels $1$ to $3$, Gaussian or not. It first appears at level~$4$, where we compute its leading constant for independent fractional Brownian motion in $d=2$: on $(\tfrac12,1)$ it is $1/(2\sqrt3)$, independent of $H$, and on $(\tfrac14,\tfrac12)$ it is given by a $ζ$-series. For fractional Brownian motion with drift, a level-$3$ error of the same order appears for $H\ge\tfrac12$. Below $\tfrac12$ the drift reaches the rate only at levels $\ge5$ (proved for $d\ge3$). The strong error is of exact order $δ^{2H-1/2}$ for fractional Brownian motion with $H\in(\tfrac12,1)$, so in mean square the weak error lies a full power of $δ$ below it. For $H\le\tfrac12$ the strong error is $O(δ^{\vartheta})$ for every $\vartheta<2H-\tfrac12$, uniformly over the class, and the exponent $2H-\tfrac12$ cannot be improved. Finally, we construct pairs of laws in the class whose mesh data have the same law but whose expected signatures differ by order $δ^{γ(H)}$. Hence no quantity computed from the mesh data has mean within $o(δ^{γ(H)})$ of the expected signature uniformly over the class.

papers.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.

papers.title: Hyperpolarity of polar foliations of codimension two
papers.abstract: We consider polar foliations of codimension two on compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces. In rank at least two, we prove that these foliations are hyperpolar, settling the remaining case of the hyperpolarity problem discussed by Lytchak. We show that, for irreducible spherical Coxeter quotients, the horizontal universal cover fails to be a spherical building precisely on the Cayley plane, where every such foliation is congruent to one of the two known homogeneous models.

papers.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
papers.abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(Λ)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $Λ$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(Λ)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $Λ$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.

papers.title: An Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method for Bures-Wasserstein Space
papers.abstract: We study composite optimization over the Bures--Wasserstein (BW) space of Gaussian measures. Our main observation is that a useful class of BW problems can be lifted into the Euclidean space of affine transport maps, such that the lifted problems can be solved efficiently using accelerated proximal gradient methods. For objectives whose smooth and nonsmooth components admit convex smooth and convex proximable affine lifts, respectively, our algorithm BW-FISTA achieves minimax-optimal objective gap $O(k^{-2})$ after $k$ iterations. We verify these regularity conditions for potential and interaction energies together with common spectral regularizers, and we treat stochastic gradients under a suitable noise model. As a principal application, we consider Gaussian variational inference with a log-concave, log-smooth target. Here, the resulting entropy term is handled by an efficient, exact proximal step, and we improve the previous rate of $O(k^{-1})$ to $O(k^{-2})$. We numerically verify this predicted boost with synthetic experiments.

papers.title: Almost sure bounds and tail phases for critical non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
papers.abstract: Gu and Zhang asked for almost sure upper and lower bounds on the Taylor coefficients $a_n$ of $\exp(\sum_{k\ge1}X_kz^k/\sqrt{k})$ in the unit disc, and for the dependence of these bounds on the input tail. For independent, identically distributed, rotationally invariant complex inputs with $\mathbb E|X_1|^2=1$, we prove the universal almost sure bound $|a_n|=O((\log n)^{1/4})$. Almost surely, $\limsup_{n\to\infty}|a_n|/(\log n)^{1/4}$ is positive and finite exactly when $\mathbb E[|X_1|^2\log^+|X_1|^2]<\infty$, and is zero otherwise. For each input law, we define a deterministic scale such that, almost surely, the coefficients are bounded exactly when the scale is bounded, and tend to zero exactly when it vanishes. We also determine the almost sure logarithmic growth exponent as the maximum of contributions from collective fluctuations and individual large inputs. Explicit tails exhibit distinct thresholds for boundedness and for upper bounds at the scale in the phase criteria. Examples show that neither the leading tail nor the set of finite logarithmic moments determines the almost sure phase.

papers.title: Symplectic singularities in Relative Langlands duality for products of general linear groups
papers.abstract: It was shown by Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima that the regular perverse sheaf on the affine Grassmannian of type A is isomorphic to the ring object associated to a Gelfand-Tsetlin quiver. We use this result to identify, for any finite dimensional representation $\mathbf{N}$ of a product of general linear groups, the relative Langlands dual $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ of $T^*\mathbf{N}$ with the Coulomb branch of a suitable representation. By a result of Bellamy, this implies that $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ has symplectic singularities.

papers.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs. The evidence shows that distillation can improve selected quantum students, but benefits are task- and architecture-dependent, and several studies find negligible gains or even performance degradation. Evaluations on physical quantum hardware remain limited, with some testing individual quantum components rather than complete learning pipelines. Heterogeneous protocols and incomplete resource reporting prevent general conclusions about practical quantum advantage. We identify priorities for controlled benchmarking, noise-aware learning, reproducible evaluation, and efficient transfer between quantum and classical models.

papers.title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry. Quantum emitters were found in BNNTs spanning the entirety of the visible spectrum, including spectral regions where SPEs within hBN have not been reported. Furthermore, each tube was found to possess multiple SPEs at varying emission wavelengths along the length, exhibiting lifetimes as fast as 0.5 ns, which is about two-fold faster than the fastest hBN SPEs. Additionally, we demonstrate that surface passivation/coating mitigates blinking events, therefore increasing the emitter stability. Thus, BNNTs can function as a single structure supporting a variety of multiwavelength SPE sources, while maintaining a compact radius of ~25 nm, making them ideally suited for deterministic placement and integration within nanophotonic devices such as waveguides and interferometric filters.

papers.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
papers.abstract: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow. However, such step sizes can make training inefficient and are rarely used in practice. In this paper, we study the AT dynamics of GD with large constant step sizes. We first study GD in adversarial linear logistic regression, focusing on two aspects: where the model parameters converge (implicit bias) and how quickly the losses decrease (optimization). We then turn to neural networks training and study how the sharpness of losses evolve during AT. Our results advance the understanding of the behaviors of GD with large step sizes in AT and highlight three key differences from its behavior in Standard Training (ST): (i) the implicit bias gap between AT and ST, previously established only for small step sizes, persists for arbitrarily large constant step sizes, (ii) different from ST, there is no uniform rate of convergence for the optimization error in AT, and (iii) sharpness can exhibit two-stage dynamics that differ from the Edge-of-Stability behavior observed in ST.

papers.title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp order of discrepancy in Tusnády's problem in every fixed dimension $d\ge 2$. The largest combinatorial discrepancy of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$, extending Wei's planar result and matching Nikolov's upper bound. More strongly, with high probability, this lower bound holds simultaneously for every subset obtained by deleting at most a sufficiently small fixed fraction of a uniform $N$-point sample. We apply this geometric estimate to online thinning of two independent samples of size $n$ from an unknown common distribution, where observations must be kept or discarded upon arrival. For every fixed dimension $k\ge 1$ and expected deletion budget $ρn$, with $0<ρ<2$, we prove that the minimax expected prefix discrepancy over lower orthants is $Θ_{k,ρ}((\log n)^{k+1/2})$. In dimension one, the optimal terminal discrepancy is instead $Θ_ρ((\log\log n)^{3/2})$, giving a sharp separation between the prefix and terminal objectives. For $k\ge 2$, we obtain terminal bounds differing by a factor of $\log n$. The lower bounds are based on Gaussian small-ball estimates for box-incidence matrices, while the upper bounds use stationary Metropolis thinning and, in one dimension, a terminal cancellation procedure.

papers.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that every complete noncompact two-sided properly embedded constant mean curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal. The result holds in every dimension. We assume no bounds on curvature or volume growth. This establishes the properly embedded case of the finite-index version of do Carmo's question. For nonzero mean curvature, we use the radii of inscribed balls to define a positive weight. This weight gives a polynomial bound on weighted volume, while its reciprocal satisfies a differential inequality involving the Jacobi operator. We combine these properties with stability outside a compact set to obtain finite total area. This leads to a contradiction.

papers.title: h-dichotomies via uniform noncriticality and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families. A key difference is that noninvertibility makes the structure of the stable spaces more delicate: in our positive-half-line result, finite codimension must be imposed at every time, rather than only at the initial time. We show by an example that the latter, weaker condition is insufficient. We also study evolution families on the negative half-line, using duality to obtain corresponding characterizations in terms of dual expansiveness and dual uniform noncriticality. General growth rates are treated by a time-rescaling argument.

papers.title: Improved Index and Intersection bounds for Min-Max Geodesics
papers.abstract: In this note, we show that the sum of the Morse index and number of intersections of min-max geodesics achieving the p-widths of a closed surface are bounded above by $p$, improving a result from our previous work. A key idea is that deformations coming from vertex desingularization and eigenfunctions of the Jacobi operator on geodesics are sufficiently independent.

papers.title: Gelfand numbers of Schatten class embeddings in the quasi-Banach range
papers.abstract: We prove Conjecture 1.4 of Prochno and Strzelecki [J. Approx. Theory 277 (2022), 105736] on Gelfand numbers of embeddings between finite-dimensional Schatten classes. For $0<p\le1$ and indices bounded away from the ambient dimension by a fixed proportion, we obtain the conjectured lower bound, uniformly in the target exponent $2\le q\le\infty$. Together with the known upper estimate obtained by Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral [Math. Ann., 380(3-4):1563-1593, 2021], this gives the exact asymptotic order in the previously unresolved range. As a consequence, we obtain a complete all-index description by combining our result with the estimates of Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral and of Prochno and Strzelecki. The proof is deterministic and is based on Hilbert--Schmidt projections on rectangular matrix spaces.

papers.title: A Central Limit Theorem For Random Variables Under A Constraint
papers.abstract: We consider vectors chosen randomly from high-dimensional hypersurfaces of the form $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n: \sum_{j=1}^n V_j(x_j)=an\}$. These in general asymmetric surfaces generalize classical spheres and include unbounded and disconnected surfaces. We show that under mild assumptions as $n\to\infty$, any weighted sum of the random coordinates is asymptotically Gaussian, provided that no weight dominates. An explicit reduction in the variance compared to the unconstrained case is observed. We also study a model with penalization of deviations from the constraint, interpolating between the unconstrained and the constrained case. Our approach involves an explicit representation of the characteristic function of the constrained random variables in terms of independent random variables.

papers.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
papers.abstract: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. To introduce quantum auxiliary supervision during training, we employ a quantum neural network (QNN) or quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold network (QKAN) as an auxiliary solubility prediction head over shared Transformer representations. The auxiliary prediction loss is jointly optimized with the diffusion objective, allowing quantum auxiliary supervision to influence the learned denoising model. Once trained, protein sequences are generated entirely through classical reverse diffusion. On the CATH benchmark, DiffSequence-Q achieved the highest secondary structure recovery among the four evaluated models for complete sequence generation. Evaluation with a separately trained solubility prediction model showed that the best QNN and QKAN configurations achieved mean predicted solubility scores 14.0% and 22.7% higher than the multilayer perceptron (MLP) baseline, respectively. Experimental characterization further demonstrated biological activity across three distinct protein families. Selected defensins exhibited pronounced inhibitory activity against Aspergillus niger, while xylanases and short-chain dehydrogenases exhibited substantial enzymatic activity. Together, these results support DiffSequence-Q as a framework for integrating structural requirements and solubility targets in protein generation, with experimentally demonstrated biological activity.

papers.title: An improved minimum degree threshold for fractional clique decompositions in partite graphs
papers.abstract: We prove a Dirac-type condition for an $r$-partite graph to admit a fractional clique decomposition: every sufficiently large $r$-partite graph with $n$ vertices in each part and partite minimum degree at least $(1 - \frac{1}{30r^2}) n$ admits a fractional $K_r$-decomposition, subject to necessary divisibility conditions. This implies the same upper bound on the asymptotic minimum degree threshold for $r$-partite graphs to admit a $K_r$-decomposition, using a well-known reduction.

papers.title: Spiking neuromodulation: a linear control perspective
papers.abstract: Neuronal excitability is a nonlinear phenomenon, and the complexity of spiking experimental traces sometimes looks defeating. The present paper takes the view point that excitability is a neuromodulated property, and aims to demonstrate that the neuromodulation of spiking is amenable to the classical linear analysis tools of control theory. We illustrate the value of linear feedback analysis as an alternative to bifurcation analysis in the simple yet classical example of spiking modulation by the A-type potassium current.

papers.title: Preconditioning for the time-dependent Stokes equations: stage-weighted Radau IIA and weighted discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping
papers.abstract: We determine field-of-values equivalent preconditioners for the time-dependent Stokes equations discretized in time by stage-weighted Radau IIA Runge--Kutta time-stepping and discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping methods. By weighing each stage of the Radau IIA Runge--Kutta method differently we obtain preconditioners that are field-of-values equivalent, with constants independent of viscosity, timestep, and mesh size, to the system matrix. Similarly, by using weighted inner products in time to define the discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping method, we again obtain field-of-values equivalent preconditioners for the resulting system matrix. Numerical experiments are performed in two and three-dimensions which demonstrate robustness of the proposed preconditioners.

papers.title: Quantum enhanced beam displacement estimation: sensitivity limits, optimal probes, and measurement schemes
papers.abstract: We investigate the ultimate sensitivity limits for measuring small transverse beam displacements and identify optimal strategies that attain them, using the framework of mode parameter estimation. We contrast two families of states with different resource constraints, using Hermite-Gauss and Laguerre-Gauss mode pairs. First, for fixed total photon number states, the optimal state is identified and we show that it asymptotically approaches a rotated NOON state. The sensitivity bound is compared to that of an asymptotically optimal pure Gaussian state with fixed average photon number. Finally, we propose concrete measurement schemes using the method of moments and show that the twin-Fock state may provide a viable alternative to the rotated NOON state for this task. Our work provides a broader benchmark for developing practical strategies for spatial sensing at the quantum limit.

papers.title: Disorder-blind Mpemba acceleration of quantum state preparation
papers.abstract: Using the strong Mpemba effect to accelerate relaxation by initial-state design requires suppressing the slowest mode, which typically needs prior knowledge of the system. However, in disordered systems, this mode is sample-dependent, so a fixed preparation generally retains a slow-mode overlap. We show that a ``blind'' preparation, designed from the clean chain without knowledge of the disorder realisation or its distribution, can start farther from stationarity yet overtake a reference in typical samples of a dephased disordered XX chain. It requires only the chain geometry and the particle number. At strong dephasing, the density dynamics maps to a resistor chain, and an exact inverse-generator identity links the residual overlap to the spatial resistance profile. We find two distinct thresholds: a finite mean resistance suffices for diffusion, but the residual overlap decays as $L^{-1/2}$ with chain length $L$ only when the resistance variance is finite; rare weak links slow this decay. We predict the fraction of samples in which the blind preparation wins, which is an ensemble-level measure of its reliability. Finite-size calculations support both scaling regimes with interactions at strong dephasing. We give preparation circuits and a density readout for the residual overlap.

papers.title: Spheres with transitive families of CMC hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to investigate the following question: what geometric restrictions does the existence of a transitive family of constant mean curvature hyperspheres impose on a Riemannian metric on $\mathbb S^n$? The notion of a transitive family can be made precise through the theory of Zoll families developed by Ambrozio, Marques, and Neves. Within this framework, we partially extend their local rigidity theorem for even conformal factors on $\mathbb S^3$ to every dimension $n\ge4$, assuming each hypersphere in the minimal Zoll family has the area of a round equator. Moreover, we give a partial answer to the following higher-dimensional version of a question posed by Robert Bryant: must a metric on $\mathbb S^n$, conformal to the round metric and admitting a Zoll family of hyperspheres with a common nonzero constant mean curvature, have constant sectional curvature? Finally, we also investigate inverse problems in the spirit of Hangan, asking which metrics make a fixed family of geodesic spheres have a common prescribed mean curvature.

papers.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
papers.abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.

papers.title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
papers.abstract: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. This answers a question previously raised by the author.

papers.title: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
papers.abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.

papers.title: Low-Temperature Sampling via Equilibrium Disagreements
papers.abstract: We develop a new framework for sampling at low temperatures using Glauber dynamics. In this regime, the coexistence of competing modes (commonly referred to as phases) creates bottlenecks that can make worst-case mixing exponentially slow. The main new ingredient in our framework is to relate convergence within a phase to the geometry of disagreements between two independent configurations drawn from that phase. As applications of our approach, we consider three canonical models on random regular graphs that have been central to low-temperature sampling, and establish fast convergence from natural initialisations of Glauber dynamics for every fixed degree. We show: --- For the hard-core model on random bipartite $d$-regular graphs, Glauber dynamics initialised from either one-sided independent set mixes within the corresponding phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps throughout the non-uniqueness regime $λ>λ_c(d)$. --- For the random-cluster model on random $d$-regular graphs, for every real $q>2$, Glauber dynamics initialised from the all-in edge set mixes within the ordered phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps for all $β\geq β_c$. Similarly, Glauber dynamics initialised from the all-out edge set mixes within the disordered phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps for $β\leq β_c$. --- For the ferromagnetic Ising model on random $d$-regular graphs, Glauber dynamics initialised from all-plus or all-minus mixes within the corresponding phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps throughout the low-temperature regime $β>β_c(d)$. We also give an $n^{2+o(1)}$-time algorithm that combines phase samples into samples from the full distribution, avoiding in particular time-costly approximations of the corresponding partition functions to the target sampling accuracy.

papers.title: Shades and Convexity of Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f\colon M^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, be a smooth immersion of a closed oriented manifold, with Gauss map $ν\colon M\to\mathbf{S}^n$. For each unit vector $u$, the shade $S_u\subset M$ is the set of points where $ν$ makes an acute angle with $u$. We show that $f$ is a convex embedding if and only if every shade is contractible. More generally, if every shade is $k$-connected, then $f$ is a convex embedding provided that $n\leq 2k+1$, or $n=2k+2$ and $H_{k+1}(M;\mathbf{Z})=0$. On the other hand, for every $n\geq 2k+3$ there is a nonconvex embedding $f\colon\mathbf{S}^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$ all of whose shades are $k$-connected. These results give sharp answers to a question of H. Wente in all dimensions.

papers.title: Averages of sub-additive functions through non-Følner sequences
papers.abstract: We study the quantity $\sup_{φ\inΦ}\limsup_{n\to\infty}φ(F_n)/|F_n|$, where $\mathcal F= (F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of finite subsets of a countable amenable group, and $Φ$ is a collection of subadditive functions. Under mild conditions on $Φ$ we prove that the aforementioned quantity equals the supremum over $φ\inΦ$ of the limit of $φ(F)/|F|$ as $F$ becomes more and more invariant, multiplied by a ``Følnerness'' constant $C(\mathcal F)\in[1,\infty]$. We have $C(\mathcal F)=1$ if and only if $\mathcal F$ is Følner. A corollary of this result is that every choice of a non-Følner sequence overestimates topological and measure-theoretic entropy by the multiplicative factor $C(\mathcal F)$ (in the positive entropy case). We obtain a generalization of classical results of Goodman, Krug, and Newton, on the so-called proportionality principle for sequence entropy, and their extension by Gao, Huang, and Zhu to countable amenable groups.

papers.title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
papers.abstract: We study smooth structures on the topological manifold underlying complex projective space. We conjecture that every complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ with $n>3$ admits an exotic smooth structure. We prove two results providing strong evidence for this conjecture. First, the set of complex dimensions $n$ for which $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure has natural density one. Second, we explicitly identify $266$ congruence classes modulo $288$ such that $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure whenever $n>3$ lies in one of these classes. These classes cover more than $92\%$ of complex dimensions, improving the previously known lower bound of approximately $36\%$. We prove these results by first relating the concordance group of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ to suitable Atiyah--Hirzebruch filtration subgroups of its stable cohomotopy group, and then applying computations in chromatic homotopy theory at height $2$.

papers.title: Augmented Lagrangian methods with telescopic subproblems for MPCCs and cardinality constraints with general constraints: constraint-preserving swaps and B-stationarity
papers.abstract: We consider optimization problems with general equality and inequality constraints and partitioned cardinality constraints, which include complementarity constraints. In the augmented Lagrangian method that we consider, the bounds and the cardinality constraints are kept in the subproblems, which are solved by the Telescopic Method. The limit points of this method are B-stationary, without constraint qualifications, if the penalty parameters remain bounded, but not in general. The reason is that the swaps of the Telescopic Method pass through points at which the constraints have different values, and the corresponding variation of the penalty term grows with the penalty parameter. With unbounded penalty parameters and a derivative test outside the current face, the feasible limit points at which a linear independence constraint qualification holds are M-stationary for MPCCs. We modify the swaps, by means of a scaled Newton restoration, so that they preserve the values of the constraints, and we prove that every feasible limit point at which this constraint qualification holds is then B-stationary (S-stationary for MPCCs), whatever the behavior of the penalty parameters. Counterexamples show that the modification is necessary, even with exact solutions of the subproblems, and that the constraint qualification cannot be weakened to one of Mangasarian-Fromovitz type. In the MacMPEC collection, the method found certified S- or B-stationary points in 185 of the 193 instances, more than Algencan and the regularization method of Scholtes. In experiments with cardinality-constrained portfolios and sparse principal component analysis, the constraint-preserving swaps improved the original swaps and the methods applied to complementarity reformulations.

papers.title: Spectral Regimes of Truncated sinc-Power and Pulse-Train Kernels: Edge Exponents, Per-Edge Plunges, and the Landau-Widom Limit
papers.abstract: A signal band-limited to one rectangular band and observed through a finite window is the classical concentration problem of Slepian, Landau, Pollak, and Widom. The eigenvalues of the operator cluster near one and near zero, separated by a transition called the plunge. The plunge width grows like the logarithm of the window length, with a universal coefficient of one over pi squared set by the band-edge jump. This paper follows the clusters and the plunge as the band is deformed. An elementwise power of the kernel smooths the band edge, and the plunge gives way to a power-law edge with exponent one less than the power. Disjoint copies of the band widen the plunge in proportion to the number of band edges, as the multiple-interval theorem of Landau and Widom implies, so the coefficient is a per-edge constant. Shrinking each band to a line gives the classical finite-rank operator. Overlapping bands give a multilevel staircase, and a self-similar band gives a cluster hierarchy governed by the Cantor dimension. At the smooth edge, rescaled eigenvalues do not collapse onto one curve. The edge descriptor passes from a constant to an exponent to an integer to a fractal dimension. For the single band, classical results place all eigenfilter zeros on the unit circle, with more of them inside the band as the order rises, so the dominant eigenvectors act as lowpass filters.

papers.title: Recalibration-Aware Optimization of ZEFOZ Operating Points in $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}:\mathrm{Y}_2\mathrm{SiO}_5$ for Quantum Memories
papers.abstract: Erbium-doped solids like $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}:\mathrm{Y}_2\mathrm{SiO}_5$ have properties that make them suitable for quantum-network memories, however, their unquenched effective electronic spin causes rapid magnetic decoherence. Operating at Zero First-Order Zeeman (ZEFOZ) points allows us to mitigate this, where we evaluate the ZEFOZ landscape for Site-2 $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$ by incorporating a full-Hessian spin-Hamiltonian treatment with the anisotropic magnetic-field covariance derived from the native $^{89}\mathrm{Y}$ crystal lattice directly. Operating-point screening criteria were adopted to devise a Pareto-optimal frontier of four transition pairs to balance modeled Y-only magnetic pure-dephasing lifetimes ($T_{φ,Y}^{(2)}$) against microwave control authority. The $ε_{14}\leftrightarrowε_{15}$ transition exhibits the longest modeled Y-bath-induced quadratic pure-dephasing time, $T_{φ,Y}^{(2)}>2.2\times10^5~\mathrm{s}$, while the $ε_{12}\leftrightarrowε_{13}$ transition stood out, achieving a Rabi frequency coefficient of $1.248 \times 10^5~\mathrm{Hz/mT}$. An assumption-based Hamiltonian-uncertainty analysis demonstrates that while uncompensated deviations shift the ZEFOZ condition away from its nominal magnetic-field coordinate, the shifted operating points can be recovered via numerical vector-field recalibration. The Pareto-optimal coordinates were mathematically recovered for all sampled Hamiltonian perturbations, and the $84.1^{\mathrm{st}}$-percentile field relocations ranged from $10.95$ to $27.97~\mathrm{mT}$. The intended operation near $10~\mathrm{mK}$ must be taken into account for the suppression of Er-induced spectral diffusion through electronic-spin polarization, while the extended Y-bath pure-dephasing timescales also remain conditional on the adopted temporal-correlation model.

papers.title: On supersoluble like groups of automorphisms of compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a not necessary full automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We found sharp bounds for $|G|$ in the terms of $g$ when $G$ belongs to one of the following classes of finite groups sharing similar properties with supersoluble groups: 2-nilpotent, with the Sylow tower of supersoluble type, with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal cyclic primary subgroups, widely supersoluble, with submodular Sylow subgroups, with submodular cyclic primary subgroups and strongly supersoluble.

papers.title: Space of Geometric Gibbs Measures: Uniqueness, Ergodicity, and Teichmüller Complex Manifold Structure
papers.abstract: Building on our previous work, in which geometric Gibbs measures were introduced to complete the space of classical Gibbs measures under the Teichmüller metric, we establish the uniqueness of geometric Gibbs measures in this paper. This result completes the construction of a Teichmüller complex manifold structure on the space of all geometric Gibbs measures. Using the welding technique, we uncover a connection between geometric Gibbs measures and harmonic measures on dynamical quasicircles. This connection allows us to establish asymptotic conformal rigidity for these dynamical quasicircles. Finally, we establish a foundation for the systematic study of the ergodic properties of geometric Gibbs measures.

papers.title: Steinberg module and top-dimensional cohomology for arithmetic Chevalley groups
papers.abstract: We prove that for a Chevalley--Demazure group scheme $\mathcal{G}$ of type $G_2$, $F_4$ or $E_8$ and a Euclidean ring $\mathcal{O}$ with field of fractions $K$, the Steinberg module of $\mathcal{G}(K)$ is generated by integral apartment classes. As a consequence, the top-dimensional rational cohomology of $\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{O})$ vanishes if $\mathcal{O}$ is a ring of integers, extending results of Tóth and of Brück--Santos Rego--Sroka.

papers.title: On the elliptic regularization of maximal slope curves
papers.abstract: We consider the so-called Weighted Energy-Dissipation approximation of gradient flows in metric spaces. We prove the convergence of minimizers to maximal slope curves under assumptions that are close to those of the original existence theory for metric gradient flows. The proof relies on an energy-dissipation identity for the approximating curves and on an adaptation of a general stability result for maximal slope curves.

papers.title: New results on cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: Inspired by the work of Poljak, Bašić, Damnjanović, Stevanović, and Stošić used the Kissat SAT solver in a recent paper to systematically determine the small cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers of several families of graphs. By studying the patterns in their data, Bašić et al. formulated 15 conjectures on cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers. In this paper, we confirm 9 of their conjectures, trace confirmations of 2 more to existing literature, and, perhaps surprisingly, disprove another one.

papers.title: A Simple Approach to the Complexity of Mean Field Ising Spin Glasses
papers.abstract: The geometry of spherical spin glasses is relatively well understood, thanks in large part to the Kac-Rice formula. However, this formula does not directly apply to discrete spin systems, and much less is known mathematically about the geometry of Ising spin glasses. In this paper, we present a simple method for counting local optima and gapped states in a broad class of discrete spin glasses. To illustrate its scope, we compute the annealed complexities ("configurational entropies," in the physics language) of mixed Ising spin glasses with potentials, such as external fields, and of the Ghatak-Sherrington model. These computations recover several existing results in the mathematics and physics literature as special cases. We can also compute energy-constrained complexity, finding a critical energy threshold analogous to the spherical case, but for gapped states of pure Ising spin glasses. Finally, we use our method to establish a form of disorder persistence for gapped states, identifying a transition between $3$-spin and $4$-spin glasses.

papers.title: Modelling and analysis of a cocktail phage therapy with coinfection
papers.abstract: We analyze a delay differential model for phage therapy in which a cocktail of $n$ different types of bacteriophages, each with its own latency period, is administered and coinfection is allowed. We prove the global existence, uniqueness and nonnegativity of solutions, and the existence of an invariant region, under suitable conditions, in which the bacteria are eradicated exponentially fast. We determine the stability of the bacteria-free equilibrium in terms of the administered doses and give sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of coexistence equilibria, showing that coinfection may allow bacteria and phages to coexist even when the doses are large. For a cocktail of two phage types with the same latency period, we obtain a complete description of the biologically feasible coexistence equilibria, which may be zero, one or two. Numerical simulations illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $β=2$
papers.abstract: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $β=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by Dürr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).

papers.title: A Theoretical Analysis of a Bilevel Optimization Formulation for Combined Local-Global Optical Flow Models
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes a bilevel formulation for learning the regularization parameter of combined local-global (CLG) optical flow models. The lower-level problem computes the flow from a Lucas--Kanade data term and a quadratic or total variation (TV) regularizer, and the upper-level problem selects the parameter that minimizes the squared distance to a ground-truth flow. The setting is finite-dimensional, and a full-rank assumption makes the lower-level solution unique. For the quadratic model we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of an optimal parameter, for every optimal parameter to be positive, and for strict local optimality. For TV regularization an optimal parameter always exists, because the lower-level solution vanishes for large parameters, and we give a sufficient condition for positivity that accounts for the coupling of the two flow components through the local structure tensors. Synthetic examples illustrate the conditions, including cases in which they fail.

papers.title: Twisted Yangians of quasi-split type DI and Drinfeld type current relations
papers.abstract: We study the twisted Yangian associated with the quasi-split symmetric pair $(\mathfrak{o}_{2n}, \mathfrak{o}_{n-1}\oplus \mathfrak{o}_{n+1})$ of type DI. Working in the transposed $R$-matrix presentation of arXiv:2607.14692, we show that the generating matrix $S(u)$ admits no Gaussian decomposition. We decompose instead the matrix $\widehat{S}(u) = G\,S(u)$, where $G$ is the constant term of $S(u)$. A chain of quasi-determinantal embeddings lowers the rank within this family of pairs and ends at $(\mathfrak{o}_4,\mathfrak{o}_3)$. Together with a direct study of a degenerate block of type AI, this gives a presentation of the special twisted Yangian $SY^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{o}_{2n},\mathfrak{o}_{n-1}\oplus \mathfrak{o}_{n+1})$ by Drinfeld type current relations. The two fork nodes of the Dynkin diagram carry Drinfeld's presentation of $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. All other relations are those of split type DI, except that the Serre relation with a doubled fork node has zero right hand side. For $n\ge3$ we obtain an explicit isomorphism between the $R$-matrix presentation of Guay and Regelskis and the Drinfeld presentation of Lu and Zhang. The Drinfeld generators are expressed through the Gaussian series of $\widehat{S}(u)$. With quasi-split type AIII (Lu and Zhang), this completes the explicit comparison for the classical quasi-split types with a nontrivial diagram involution.

papers.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
papers.abstract: We prove that K3 surfaces with no rational points over the finite field with $q$ elements exist if and only if $q \leq 11$. Our approach applies linear programming techniques to improve on generic sphere packing bounds for the discriminants of even rootless definite lattices. These bounds are applied to constrain the possible zeta functions of K3 surfaces with no rational points via the Artin--Tate formula. The remaining cases are ruled out by direct analysis of primitive embeddings of particular lattices into Niemeier lattices.

papers.title: Global solutions for continuous-time Burgers equations and infinite-volume polymer measures
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic Burgers equation on the whole space, driven by space-homogeneous Gaussian noises that are white in time and colored in space, for both positive and zero viscosity. We show that in dimension one, for any fixed average velocity, there is a unique ergodic global solution to the Burgers equation for all nonnegative viscosities, and that the One Force---One Solution principle holds. We also describe the basin of attraction and show that these global solutions are one-point pullback attractors. Moreover, the viscous global solution converges to the inviscid global solution as the viscosity tends to zero. Our technique relies on the study of polymer measures; accordingly, we establish the existence and uniqueness of infinite-volume polymer measures in a given asymptotic direction, as well as their convergence to semi-infinite minimizers in the zero-temperature limit. We also establish the existence part of all these results in arbitrary dimension larger than one.

papers.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
papers.abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos, in Katriel's differential equations. From the elementary reactions, without reference to the differential equations, we derive a deterministic map $F_τ$ for a large population updated in rounds of length $τ$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. Katriel's equations are recovered as $τ\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, the map goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $β/γ=46$, $μ/γ=0.002$, $γτ=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. Chaos is supported by independent indicators: a positive Lyapunov exponent with Kaplan--Yorke dimension $1.81$, a matching correlation dimension, the 0-1 test ($K\approx1$ exactly in the window), a broadband spectrum, ordinal-pattern complexity, sensitive dependence on initial conditions and dense saddle periodic orbits. One-stage contagion, $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle: the round structure turns this oscillation into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is thus a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating, not an artefact of discretisation.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
papers.abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.

papers.title: Simple Modules over Leavitt Path Algebras Generated by Indicator Functions on Paths
papers.abstract: Let E be an arbitrary graph, K a field, and D the set of boundary paths of E consisting of both infinite paths and finite paths ending at singular vertices. The space KD of K-valued functions on D is a right module over the Leavitt path algebra LK(E). For a non- empty set S ? D that is strongly connected and closed under adding and deleting initial segments, we study the submodule N_S = 1_S.LK(E) generated by the indicator function of S. Let S_0 be the set of vertices lying on the paths in S. We show that N_S is simple if and only if S contains no breaking vertex of the hereditary saturated set H = E0 nS0. In particular, when S contains only infinite paths or when E is a row- finite graph, NS is a simple module. Up to isomorphism, the simple module NS depends only on S_0. When S is an infinite set of paths, the simple module NS is neither graded nor projective. The left module LK(E)1_S, obtained by twisting the action through the involution of LK(E), is simple exactly when NS is, and, when S is infinite, it is not isomorphic to any of the Chen simple modules. For the rose graph R_n with n ? 2 petals, we show that LK(R_n)1_S is isomorphic to one of the twisted Chen modules constructed by Nam, Srivastava and Vien, and to none of the other simple modules in their list. Moreover, when S is not a single vertex, the simple module NS is finitely presented if and only if only finitely many edges of E have both source and range in S_0; in particular, every simple module N_S is finitely presented when E is a finite graph. Finally, we determine when the analogous module generated by an indicator function over the Cohn path algebra CK(E) is simple. 1.

papers.title: Almost S-GCD domains: localization, class groups, and extensions
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be an integral domain and let $S\subseteq D\setminus\{0\}$ be multiplicative. We study the condition that, for each nonzero $a,b\in D$, some $(a^n,b^n)_v$ is $S$-principal. A power estimate extends this binary condition to arbitrary finite families and permits synchronization of exponents. We describe the obstruction to descent from the AGCD domain $D_S$ by bounded $S$-torsion and by a finiteness condition on intersections of principal ideals. For an almost Prüfer $v$-multiplication domain, the almost $S$-GCD property, the AGCD property of $D_S$, and torsion of the $S$-class group are equivalent. In Krull domains this gives a criterion in terms of the divisor classes of height-one primes meeting $S$, and finite rational class rank reduces the multiplicative set to one element. We prove conductor transfer without a principal-contraction hypothesis, polynomial transfer in several settings, a normalization homeomorphism away from $S$, and a finite-principal-cover criterion with a Picard-group obstruction. Explicit examples distinguish localization, bounded descent, and the global and sublocal conditions.

papers.title: Fluctuations, Moderate and Large Deviations about Hydrodynamic Limits of Space-Time Hawkes Processes
papers.abstract: We study Gaussian fluctuations, moderate and large deviations around the high-density hydrodynamic limit of critical and nearly critical space-time Hawkes processes initialized by a prescribed Poisson field of past events, with no subsequent immigration. Under a finite mean reproduction delay and centered displacements with finite spatial covariance, a positive cluster-transform estimate yields a distribution-valued central limit theorem (CLT) and a moderate deviation principle (MDP) throughout the moderate range. For finite nonzero mass of the initial profile, we obtain a full large deviation principle (LDP) for the space-time event measure in the vague topology; its good rate function is a quadratic branching-control energy with a prescribed initial trace and a finite-mass domain. The lower bound uses an explicit approximation by smooth reproduction controls, and the upper bound uses a microscopic exponential martingale and a global generator approximation. We distinguish exact-mean centering from PDE centering and compute deterministic bias corrections under second delay and fourth spatial moments. For a factorized heavy-tail power-law delay, we establish the CLT, MDP, and full measure-valued LDP for the space-time measure, with finite nonzero mass of the initial profile for the LDP. Its fractional control energy retains the source generated by the prescribed past. A source-preserving regularization proves approximation of every finite-action measure.
